author: Eric Berne
provenance: Structured reference material (paraphrased, no verbatim reproduction).

slices.summary: Definition of a transaction; three transaction types (complementary, crossed, ulterior); examples of each. Complementary = stable because the response comes from the addressed state and returns to the sender state. Crossed = breaks the conversation when the response comes from an unexpected state.
slices.usageNote: Core teaching material for Ch2. Use ONLY the complementary and crossed material; ulterior is named as a forward-pointer only.

slices.summary: Ch2 in the ChapterFlow mapping covers complementary and crossed only. Ulterior, games, payoffs, life positions belong to Ch3 and Ch4.
slices.usageNote: Scope guard. Reject any drift toward game definitions or stroke economics.

slices.summary: Reserved Ch1 names must not reuse: Priya, Marcus, Halden, Elena, Noor, Chidi, Alvarez, Danielle, Jamal, Sam, Rebecca. Ch2 introduces a new cast: Tomas, Aiya, Coach Reyes, Diego, Olivia, Kenji, Yusuf, Mara, Larsson, Bea.

Hard-depth tension: the diagram is diagnostic, not prescriptive. The three moves available on a cross (recross deliberately, accept and name it, wait) are situational decisions the model does not make for the reader.

forbiddenContent: Verbatim or near-verbatim reproduction of Berne's prose.
Any unpacking of ulterior transactions (Ch3 territory).
Any reference to specific game names (NIGYSOB, Why Don't You Yes But, etc.) — they belong to Chs 3, 5, 6, 7, 8.
Any stroke economics, payoff theory, or life-position language (Ch4).
Any reuse of Ch1 character names.
